Let \(P\) be the apex. Label the other base vertices \(B,C,D\) so that \(ABCD\) is the square, with \(A\) the labeled vertex. Let the three marked midpoints be

- \(M\in AB\),

The shaded cutting plane is the plane through \(M,N,R\). Notice that its section with the pyramid is a pentagon: it also meets \(PB\) at its midpoint and \(PC\) at a point \(T\) with \(CT:TP=3:1\).

### 1. Normalize the pyramid

Since volume ratios are preserved by affine scaling, take the base to be the unit square

\[
A=(0,0,0),\quad B=(1,0,0),\quad C=(1,1,0),\quad D=(0,1,0),
\]

and let the apex be \(P=(p,q,1)\).

The marked points are

\[
M=\left(\frac12,0,0\right),\qquad
N=\left(0,\frac12,0\right),\qquad
R=\left(\frac p2,\frac{q+1}{2},\frac12\right).
\]

The plane through these points has equation

\[
x+y-(p+q)z=\frac12.
\]

Since \(A\) gives \(0<\frac12\), the part containing \(A\) satisfies

\[
x+y-(p+q)z\le \frac12.
\]

### 2. Find the horizontal cross-sectional areas

At height \(z\), the pyramid has a square cross-section of side \(1-z\). Write

\[
x=pz+u,\qquad y=qz+v,
\]

where \(0\le u,v\le 1-z\). The cutting inequality becomes

\[
u+v\le \frac12.
\]

Thus the area of the part containing \(A\) at height \(z\) is

\[
S(z)=
\begin{cases}
\dfrac18, & 0\le z\le \dfrac12,\\[6pt]
(1-z)^2-\dfrac12\left(\dfrac32-2z\right)^2,
& \dfrac12\le z\le \dfrac34,\\[8pt]
(1-z)^2, & \dfrac34\le z\le1.
\end{cases}
\]

Therefore, in the normalized pyramid,

\[
\begin{aligned}
V_A
&=\int_0^{1/2}\frac18\,dz
+\int_{1/2}^{3/4}\left(-z^2+z-\frac18\right)dz
+\int_{3/4}^1(1-z)^2\,dz\\
&=\frac1{16}+\frac5{192}+\frac1{192}
=\frac3{32}.
\end{aligned}
\]

The normalized pyramid has volume

\[
\frac13(1)(1)=\frac13,
\]

so the desired volume fraction is

\[
\frac{V_A}{V_{\text{pyramid}}}
=\frac{3/32}{1/3}
=\frac9{32}.
\]
